package_info.why_malicious: SHARPTEXT is a malicious browser extension developed by the SharpTongue (Kimsuky) threat actor. It is designed to steal webmail credentials and session data from Gmail and AOL users, exfiltrating sensitive information to attacker-controlled infrastructure. The extension operates covertly, targeting user privacy and security.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the extension monitors web requests to Gmail and AOL webmail, injects code to extract page content (including emails and credentials), and exfiltrates this data via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and exfiltrating webmail content is a clear violation of user privacy and security. The extension abuses browser APIs to steal sensitive data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate browser extensions should not access or transmit private webmail content without user consent. This behavior is covert and malicious.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some password managers or security extensions may access webmail pages to provide user features, but always with explicit user consent and without exfiltration.
key_indicators: Network requests to external, non-legitimate domains
Use of browser APIs for data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: User is tricked into installing the SHARPTEXT browser extension.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious extension is loaded in the browser.

attack_chain.action: Extension monitors user activity for visits to Gmail or AOL webmail.
Extension injects code to extract webmail content and credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is collected from the user's session.

attack_chain.action: Collected data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to stolen webmail data.

behavioral_signatures: Browser extension accessing webmail page content
Unusual network requests from browser extensions to unknown domains
Use of browser APIs (webRequest, tabs, storage) for data collection and exfiltration
file_indicators: Presence of SHARPTEXT extension in browser extension directories
background.js or content scripts with code referencing mail.google.com or mail.aol.com
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POST requests from browser to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., attacker-c2.com/collect)
Unusual traffic patterns from browser processes to non-standard endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor installed browser extensions for suspicious permissions and behaviors, such as accessing webmail content or making network requests to unknown domains. Analyze extension code for references to webmail services and data exfiltration routines. Use network monitoring to detect outbound connections from browser processes to attacker infrastructure.
